about: 2-fer rule changes and the parks each one touches (Brandon Nov 9 2026, 4:37-4:42 PM CST: 'only redo the parts that changed'; KISS). A saved pair result is reused unless one of its two parks changed (outline, record ids, POTA pin / name, line) or a change below covers one of the parks. Add one entry per rule change: id (never reuse an id), when, why, and scope = {states: ['US-KY', 'CA-ON', ...], kinds: [words in the POTA park type, e.g. 'Wild and Scenic River'], flags: ['bad-pin', 'line']} or 'all' (every pair: emergency only). Emergency switch without an entry: KPC_FERS_FULL=1. The areas workflow also does ONE full area per run, round-robin (.github/fers-areas.json full_cycle_days). Nov 9 evening (KZ4CP 5:41 PM CST): a scope may also list park refs, 'parks': ['US-1234', ...]: only those parks are re-matched (their states are read again, every other park there keeps its result; for 2-fers every pair with a named park is tested again, so the parks touching it are rechecked too). A scope that lists nothing means ALL; a change that touches no park says scope 'none'.

changes.why: a park with a bad POTA pin (pin00 / 0,0) is tested by its saved record ids, never around its pin (run 42649544758)

When both parks already have an official agency outline, that layer is government or public land, so a blank owner field is not a hold. A blank owner whose outline is not from an official agency layer and is not an approximate or point-circle outline still cannot be a candidate.

Approximate outlines (picture traces and point-circles) do not block a 2-fer. The pair is an approximate 2-fer, drawn thinner and in a different color, with a note that it is not the official boundary and needs more research. WDPA / Protected Planet outlines are never a public 2-fer source.
A picture-trace outline never replaces an official outline already on file. Two parks that join the exact same official records go to the person-review list, not the candidate list.

Review fixes. Every pass reads a blocked-host layer from the key's saved copy; a missing saved copy holds the pair with a reason, and Wild and Scenic corridors come from saved records or the pair is held. Two parks on the same official records are an approximate 2-fer only when both POTA pins are inside the shared outline; otherwise the pair is held as a likely join to fix (pins and records listed on the row). Record ids are compared with their area and source; an outline with no source label is not official; a failed read never leaves a partial outline. A state feeds 2-fers only when its own index row was built on the current key rules.

A trail or river stretch counts only when at least 25 metres of the line run inside the other park (was no minimum). Pieces of one line that touch are measured together, to the line's real end. A line whose whole saved copy is under 25 metres is a broken copy: its pairs are held as not sure, never dropped. In a trail or river row the park that is not the line is graded by the current key like an area half (a key pin drops the row). A row's own stretch length is kept apart, so copies of other rows no longer shrink it.
